newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITV plans winter offensive ahead of C5 launch.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITV plans winter offensive ahead of C5 launch.

text.p: Britain's ITV commercial television network on Monday unveiled a 210 million stg winter schedule designed to boost audiences ahead of the March 1997 launch of competitor Channel 5.

ITV network director Marcus Plantin said ITV aimed to build on what he called a "damned good autumn" in which its peaktime audience share had climbed to 42.3 percent last month, a lead of some nine percent over closest rival BBC 1.
"We are investing 80 million stg in drama - a record for this time of year and a figure that is some 75 percent of the annual Channel 5 budget," he told a news conference.

Channel 5, a new national commercial terrestrial channel, will launch on March 30. It will have an annual budget of some 110 million stg and media analysts expect it to capture around five percent of all viewing.
It is owned by a consortium of British media groups Pearson and United News & Media, U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus and Luxembourg-based broadcaster CLT.

ITV, the network comprising 15 regional companies such as London's Carlton and Granada in north-west England, has come under fire in recent years for what some critics had said was a lacklustre schedule.
But Plantin said the network was now out of the doldrums and its winter 1997 schedule would reinforce the message.
ITV's drama offering ranges from classical adaptations such as "Rebecca" and "Jane Eyre" through to established favourites like "A Touch of Frost".

The network will also further increase its commitment to soap opera, screening a third weekly episode of "Emmerdale" from the New Year. ITV plans to launch a fourth weekly episode of "Coronation Street" later this month.
ITV will in March begin its coverage of Formula One motor racing, having outbid the BBC for the rights.

Formula One is set to become a mainstay of weekend scheduling, ITV screening coverage of pre-race practice on Saturdays followed by the race live and a highlights package on Sundays for each of the 16 grands prix.
